title: Celeritas: Out-of-Core Based Unsupervised Graph Neural Network via Cross-Layer Computing 2024
problem: Training large unsupervised GNNs on massive real-world graph datasets exceeds host memory capacity and demands excessive I/O migration between host memory and storage, resulting in long training times and impractical computational requirements.
motivation: Efficiently processing large-scale graphs is essential for applications like drug discovery, recommendation systems, node classification, and edge prediction.
method: Celeritas is a fully out-of-core framework co-designing GNN algorithms with storage systems. It introduces a partial combination operation enabling cross-layer computing to perform future embedding computations using in-memory data, eliminating I/O. The framework jointly optimizes data locality of embeddings and edges with a new loading order, and proposes a two-level sampling scheme with partition algorithm to further reduce data migration and computation overhead.
key_novelty: Cross-layer computing that enables future embedding computations across GNN layers using in-memory data to eliminate I/O migration.
contributions: Partial combination operation enabling cross-layer computing for embedding updates across GNN layers
New loading order strategy jointly optimizing data locality of embeddings and edges
Two-level sampling scheme with partition algorithm reducing data migration while maintaining accuracy
Complete out-of-core framework achieving 44.76-73.85% training time reduction on single machines
primary_theme: Out-of-core GNN training acceleration via cross-layer computing
